scientific.integrity: The proof reconstructs the square-zero obstruction directly from Kanazawa's published Picard basis and cubic intersection form, then applies the elementary pullback property for divisors from a curve. No finite experiment or unproved classification is used.
limitations: The theorem excludes morphisms to projective curves but does not exclude rational maps that require birational modification to become morphisms.
The argument is specific to the Picard-rank-two intersection form of Kanazawa's non-Gorenstein minus phase.
No classification of the full nef or movable cone is asserted.

title: Kanazawa's flopped gCICY has no fibration over a curve
